description: I need a quick script at /home/user/bin/diskmon.sh that checks if any mounted filesystem is over 80% usage and exits 1 if so, 0 otherwise. Just df parsing basically — gonna hook it into our alerting cron. Doesn't need to output anything, just the exit code.
truth:
Initial state:
    - /home/user/bin/ directory exists and is writable.
    - /home/user/bin/diskmon.sh does not exist.
    - Standard coreutils available including df, awk, grep, etc.
    - System has at least one mounted filesystem (/, and possibly /tmp, /home, etc.).
    - Current disk usage varies but at least one filesystem exists to check.

    Expected final state:
    - /home/user/bin/diskmon.sh exists and is executable (has +x permission).
    - Running `bash /home/user/bin/diskmon.sh` OR `/home/user/bin/diskmon.sh` completes without error.
    - If any mounted filesystem shows >=80% usage in df output, script exits with code 1.
    - If all mounted filesystems show <80% usage, script exits with code 0.
    - Script produces no stdout (or minimal/no output) — exit code is the signal.

    Invariants:
    - Script must parse actual df output, not hardcode an exit value.
    - Must check real mounted filesystems, not a fake/stub check.

    Anti-shortcut guards:
    - Script must contain "df" somewhere (grep -q 'df' /home/user/bin/diskmon.sh returns 0).
    - Script must NOT simply `exit 0` or `exit 1` unconditionally without any df check — verified by checking script contains conditional logic (if/test/[/awk-based exit) alongside df invocation.
